column16: Provisional direct match: modern terrestrial Roman-inspired OPC/fly-ash/sand mortar; quicklime 7.5-15 mass%; quicklime-free controls; controlled 0.5 mm re-mated crack; 30-day water-flow endpoint. Human adjudication is required before Tier A can count.

exact_locator: Provisional direct candidate: modern bridge-deck concrete with 0%, 2%, and 4% quicklime, controlled 100–550 µm cracks, cyclic exposure, and internal crack-depth water-flow testing; thesis is one lineage with S26 and requires expert adjudication of the selected-specimen flow design.

Government final report of the same Utah State quicklime bridge-deck experiment as S25; pp. 44–49 document falling-head water flow/permeability, pp. 51–52 controlled crack widths, and pp. 75–80 results. Count once with S25, not as an independent replication.

Open doctoral thesis studies hot-mixing, free lime, pore structure, and observed crack healing in conservation mortars, but does not expose a controlled functional water-flow recovery comparison matching the target.
Hot-mixed versus lime-putty mortars with pozzolans; fresh/hardened property and durability comparison, but no controlled crack-healing or functional water-flow endpoint.
Hot-lime construction-material thesis with physical/chemical durability work; no qualifying controlled crack-healing water-transport endpoint.

Open lime-type study includes blocky quicklime but reports material properties rather than controlled post-crack functional recovery.
Open thesis on advanced lime mortars and microbial/carbonation healing; engineered/additive system and not the target hot-mix quicklime intervention.
Natural-hydraulic-lime self-healing concrete under cyclic compression; no explicit quicklime/hot-mixing intervention or functional water-flow endpoint in the accessible record.
